summary: Dillahunty’s revisable, welfare-centered humanism outperformed Slick’s foundational Christian critique, whose serious grounding objections remained insufficiently connected to comparative practical superiority.

pro.text: secular humanism is about human flourishing
pro.context: Dillahunty identifies flourishing and empirically investigated human interests as the proposed common domain for comparing the two worldviews.

con.text: we use harm to judge whether consequences are good or bad
con.context: Slick challenges welfare consequentialism to justify its evaluative criterion without merely repeating that harmful consequences are morally disfavored.

pro-comparative-flourishing-standard.words: Human flourishing, informed by reality and methods likely to identify human interests accurately, supplies a practical domain for comparing secular humanism with Christianity.
pro-comparative-flourishing-standard.critique: Strongest feature: The move establishes an intelligible comparative domain by connecting flourishing, ascertainable interests, factual investigation, and accuracy-oriented methods directly to the secular route’s central evaluative burden. Principal limitation: Its practical plausibility does not demonstrate that both worldviews genuinely share this standard, nor that empirically accessible interests exhaust every consideration relevant to a comprehensive comparison. Live burden: The case still must justify privileging flourishing, specify its components and distribution, and show that the proposed method discriminates reliably between competing interpretations of human welfare. Locked score: The strong band reflects excellent relevance, stable formulation, and coherent methodological direction, moderated by incomplete foundational justification and limited evidence that the proposed standard is sufficient rather than merely useful.

pro-relative-comparison-without-absolute.words: Because Christian salvation claims also concern human interests, meaningful comparison remains possible without absolute certainty or an exceptionless normative standard.
pro-relative-comparison-without-absolute.critique: Strongest feature: The move incisively observes that salvation and gospel claims still concern what benefits persons, thereby preserving a comparative foothold even when deeper metaphysical foundations remain disputed. Principal limitation: Calling God irrelevant moves too quickly from the relevance of human interests to the dispensability of a divine relationship that Christianity may regard as constitutive of flourishing. Live burden: The argument must distinguish epistemic certainty from normative absoluteness and explain which comparative conclusions remain warranted when rival accounts define human good in substantially different terms. Locked score: The strong band recognizes direct burden contact, useful resistance to an excessive certainty demand, and a recoverable conclusion, while reflecting rhetorical overreach, conceptual compression, and underdeveloped engagement with Christianity’s strongest account.

pro-contextual-revisable-moral-method.words: Secular humanism can revise judgments with new information and evaluate exceptional circumstances contextually instead of relying only on unexplained fixed prohibitions.
pro-contextual-revisable-moral-method.critique: Strongest feature: The disaster example concretely demonstrates why morally relevant circumstances, reasons, and possible exceptions matter, giving the secular method an intelligible advantage over an isolated bare prohibition. Principal limitation: One compelling illustration cannot establish general methodological superiority, because sophisticated rule-based traditions may treat prohibitions as defeasible principles embedded within broader interpretive and justificatory structures. Live burden: The method must articulate the welfare criterion, decision procedure, evidentiary thresholds, and safeguards that prevent contextual flexibility from becoming selective rationalization or inconsistent application. Locked score: The upper strong band reflects explicit qualification, stable terminology, excellent central relevance, and a well-chosen counterexample, tempered by an implicit decision framework and insufficient comparison with stronger Christian moral reasoning.

pro-peace-equality-consequence-grounding.words: Peace and cooperation benefit human life, while secular commitments to equality, autonomy, and flourishing strongly oppose slavery and murder.
pro-peace-equality-consequence-grounding.critique: Strongest feature: The move connects abstract secular commitments with concrete practical consequences, showing how equality, autonomy, cooperation, and flourishing can jointly support opposition to slavery and murder. Principal limitation: The categorical assertion that nothing within secular humanism could instruct killing or enslavement exceeds what naming these values establishes, especially where values conflict or applications become contested. Live burden: The case must explain priority rules among autonomy, equality, aggregate welfare, and defensive necessity, then compare their historical and institutional reliability with Christian alternatives. Locked score: The strong band recognizes clear practical relevance, coherent value-to-consequence reasoning, and meaningful motion contact, while incorporating the unsupported universal exclusion, missing qualifications, and limited evidence for comparative reliability across difficult cases.

pro-scriptural-conflict-resolution-failu.words: Informed Christians deriving mutually exclusive salvation doctrines from the same Bible reveal a serious practical weakness in Christian conflict-resolution methods.
pro-scriptural-conflict-resolution-failu.critique: Strongest feature: The move supplies a pointed internal test of Christian reliability by focusing on informed interpreters who share scripture and salvation as a goal yet reach contradictory conclusions. Principal limitation: A single doctrinal disagreement does not establish comprehensive methodological failure, because the case leaves its representativeness, causal diagnosis, and comparison with secular disagreement insufficiently developed. Live burden: The argument must examine proposed Christian adjudication methods, establish persistence across representative central disputes, and demonstrate that secular procedures resolve analogous conflicts more reliably. Locked score: The strong band reflects a concrete counterexample, stable formulation, substantial charity, and direct practical relevance, moderated by incomplete generalization, limited evidentiary development, and the absence of a controlled comparative baseline.

con-comparative-self-refutation-threshol.words: A genuinely self-refuting worldview is necessarily inferior, at least intellectually, to a competing worldview that avoids the same internal defeat.
con-comparative-self-refutation-threshol.critique: Strongest feature: The conditional threshold is logically powerful and appropriately bounded: if one worldview genuinely defeats the intellectual foundations required to assert it, comparative inferiority follows in that respect. Principal limitation: Establishing the threshold does not establish that secular humanism actually self-refutes, nor that Christianity avoids equivalent internal difficulties or performs better across the motion’s practical domains. Live burden: The Christian case must derive a specific contradiction from secular commitments, defend every bridge in that derivation, and connect foundational consistency to flourishing and decision-making outcomes. Locked score: The strong band recognizes exceptional clarity, sound conditional force, and direct support for a subsidiary burden, while reserving completion for the unproven application and broader comparative bridge.

con-naturalism-cognition-trust-objection.words: If cognition is wholly physically caused, secular naturalism must explain reliable logical inference, whereas Christianity grounds rational capacity in minds bearing God’s image.
con-naturalism-cognition-trust-objection.critique: Strongest feature: The objection identifies a genuine epistemological burden by asking how physically realized cognition can reliably track mind-independent logical relations rather than merely produce causally determined responses. Principal limitation: It assumes without sufficient argument that physical causation undermines justification, while the appeal to divine image likewise does not independently explain reliable access, error, or cognitive calibration. Live burden: The case must show incompatibility between causal embodiment and truth-tracking, then demonstrate that Christian anthropology provides a less circular, more predictive account of successful and unsuccessful inference. Locked score: The mixed band reflects high relevance and a clear contrast between naturalist and Christian pictures, but also an unstable causation-to-defeat transition, sparse warrant, and an asserted theological alternative.

con-science-presuppositions-foundation.words: Science presupposes logic and nature’s uniformity and cannot establish every precondition through its own methods, leaving secular humanism with a foundational obligation.
con-science-presuppositions-foundation.critique: Strongest feature: The move accurately distinguishes scientific inquiry from justification of every presupposition it employs, especially logical validity and expectations concerning nature’s regularity. Principal limitation: Showing that science cannot experimentally prove all its preconditions neither reduces secular justification to unsupported faith nor establishes that Christianity uniquely grounds those preconditions. Live burden: The argument must specify the required kind of justification, compare secular pragmatic, abductive, and realist accounts, and derive logic and uniformity from Christian commitments without circularity. Locked score: The strong threshold band reflects a clear, important foundational challenge with stable terms and direct central relevance, moderated by an underdefined justificatory demand, overstated secular conclusion, and missing comparative demonstration.

con-consequentialism-standard-circularit.words: Consequentialism needs a non-circular basis for classifying outcomes as good or harmful rather than using harm reduction to justify itself.
con-consequentialism-standard-circularit.critique: Strongest feature: The move presses an indispensable normative question: consequence-sensitive reasoning requires some defensible criterion for identifying good, bad, harmful, and beneficial outcomes. Principal limitation: Its circularity diagnosis treats reliance on harm too schematically, because welfare criteria may receive constitutive, experiential, contractual, or reflective justification beyond verbal repetition. Live burden: The objection must distinguish vicious circularity from unavoidable coherence among basic values, engage the strongest justification of conscious interests, and show that Christian grounding avoids parallel dependence on foundational commitments. Locked score: The upper strong band reflects excellent central relevance, coherent conditional pressure, and substantial diagnostic value, tempered by insufficient proof that every secular welfare criterion is circular and limited engagement with available normative bridges.

con-new-testament-objective-moral-standa.words: Christian ethics claims an objective standard in New Testament revelation and distinguishes its governing principles from abrogated Old Testament laws.
con-new-testament-objective-moral-standa.critique: Strongest feature: The move clearly identifies the proposed Christian moral source and narrows the relevant revelation to New Testament principles rather than leaving the ethical standard wholly unspecified. Principal limitation: Labeling revelation objective does not establish divine authorship, interpretive reliability, normative authority, or consistent application, while the asserted abrogation boundary remains largely undefended. Live burden: The case must authenticate the source, explain how divine character generates duties, resolve textual disagreements, and demonstrate practical superiority over context-sensitive welfare assessment. Locked score: The mixed band reflects substantial relevance, a recoverable foundation claim, and useful scope clarification, but also missing warrants at every decisive bridge from document to revelation, revelation to obligation, and obligation to dependable judgment.

con-biblical-love-flourishing.words: Christian flourishing consists in proper worship, humility, and biblical obedience expressed through love of God and one’s neighbor.
con-biblical-love-flourishing.critique: Strongest feature: The reply supplies substantive Christian content by defining flourishing through worship, humility, and neighbor-love rather than accepting a purely temporal or preference-based welfare conception. Principal limitation: It presupposes that the Bible is God’s word and that proper worship constitutes flourishing, while neither comparing practical outcomes nor answering the highlighted scriptural disagreement. Live burden: The account must defend its theological premises, explain how love resolves conflicting commands and interpretations, and show superior consequences or decision procedures across the motion’s domains. Locked score: The mixed band recognizes a clear, stable, and relevant alternative conception, but reflects its assumed foundations, incomplete responsiveness, absent comparative evidence, and failure to resolve the practical reliability challenge.

pro-logic-presupposition-suffices.words: Presupposing logic without an ultimate divine account does not, by itself, demonstrate that secular reasoning is false, unreliable, or internally defective.
pro-logic-presupposition-suffices.critique: Strongest feature: The reply precisely blocks an invalid inference from lacking a further metaphysical account of logic to having a false or defective practical reasoning framework. Principal limitation: This successful diagnostic denial does not provide the positive reliability account requested elsewhere, so it answers one entailment while leaving a broader epistemological challenge active. Live burden: The secular case must explain how logical principles are recognized, how reasoning errors are detected, and why its checking practices warrant confidence without promising certainty. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional directness, explicit concession, excellent calibration, and decisive contact with the alleged defect, while retaining a modest deduction because rebutting insufficiency is not equivalent to completing the affirmative account of reliability.

pro-fallible-brains-recognize-logic.words: Fallible brains do not create logical truths; people can recognize mind-independent logical relations even though particular reasoning episodes may fail.
pro-fallible-brains-recognize-logic.critique: Strongest feature: The reply cleanly separates production from recognition and candidly concedes individual fallibility, thereby avoiding the unnecessary claim that rational cognition requires an infallibility guarantee. Principal limitation: Recognition remains more asserted than explained, leaving unresolved how physically embodied thinkers reliably access mind-independent logical truths and distinguish genuine insight from systematic error. Live burden: The account must connect cognitive mechanisms, logical constraints, corrective practices, and successful prediction into a non-question-begging explanation of practical truth-tracking. Locked score: The strong band reflects stable terminology, intellectual calibration, substantial direct responsiveness, and a coherent conceptual distinction, moderated by the missing reliability mechanism, limited evidentiary support, and incomplete engagement with the foundational version of the objection.

pro-corroborated-fallible-reasoning.words: Logic, experienced reality, and independent corroboration can test reasoning practically while preserving the possibility that every investigator remains mistaken.
pro-corroborated-fallible-reasoning.critique: Strongest feature: The reply offers a concrete fallibilist method—logical testing, experiential contact, and independent scientific affirmation—while expressly preserving the possibility of individual or collective error. Principal limitation: Intersubjective agreement can reproduce shared distortions, and the method does not fully answer whether its standards and observations ultimately connect with mind-independent truth. Live burden: The secular account must explain independence, error correction, predictive success, and adversarial replication sufficiently to distinguish reliable convergence from merely coordinated belief. Locked score: The strong band reflects excellent calibration, practical specificity, stable scope, and substantial responsiveness to the cognition challenge, while recognizing that operational reliability does not by itself settle ultimate circularity or provide a complete metaphysical foundation.

con-universal-logic-universal-mind.words: Universal abstract logical principles may imply a universal mind, which Christianity proposes as their foundation while denying comparable secular resources.
con-universal-logic-universal-mind.critique: Strongest feature: The reply offers a positive metaphysical candidate rather than merely criticizing secularism, connecting the universality of abstract logical principles with a hypothesized universal mind. Principal limitation: The speaker expressly skips crucial steps, and universality alone does not establish mentality, personal agency, Christianity, or the claimed absence of secular accounts. Live burden: The inference must defend each transition from abstract necessity to mind, from universal mind to the Christian God, and from that God to human epistemic access. Locked score: The mixed band reflects cautious inferential wording, clear foundational relevance, and an identifiable explanatory proposal, but also major omitted bridges, weak comparative support, and an overconfident assertion that Christianity completes the account without difficulty or remainder evidence.

pro-objective-value-relative-ethics.words: Objective assessment relative to an identified value differs from an exceptionless absolute rule and need not depend on cultural preference.
pro-objective-value-relative-ethics.critique: Strongest feature: The reply makes an important and logically stable distinction between objective assessment relative to a specified value and rules claimed to apply absolutely without contextual exception. Principal limitation: Clarifying conditional objectivity does not justify the governing value itself, so the foundational challenge concerning why flourishing possesses moral authority remains substantially unanswered. Live burden: The secular case must defend its selected values through facts about conscious interests, agency, reciprocity, or reflective consistency and explain how conflicts among them are adjudicated. Locked score: The upper strong band reflects conceptual precision, explicit qualification, charitable contact with the opposing concern, and strong relevance, moderated by incomplete responsiveness to the value-authority question and the absence of a substantive normative foundation.

pro-ultimate-origin-outside-humanism-sco.words: A practical secular framework can employ reliable logical principles without explaining their ultimate origin, just as evolution need not explain abiogenesis.
pro-ultimate-origin-outside-humanism-sco.critique: Strongest feature: The evolution-and-abiogenesis analogy lucidly distinguishes a framework’s operative explanatory task from a separate ultimate-origin inquiry, thereby justifying a narrower reliability-focused response. Principal limitation: Because the motion compares worldviews, declaring foundations outside secular humanism’s job may narrow the opposing demand excessively and does not establish their irrelevance to comparative adequacy. Live burden: The reply must define secular humanism’s intended scope, supply practical reliability warrants, and explain whether a broader secular worldview can address the metaphysical residue. Locked score: The very strong band reflects an exceptionally clear justified reframe, stable scope distinction, memorable explanatory analogy, and direct contact with both foundational moves, tempered by underengagement with the debate’s worldview-level framing.

con-flourishing-goal-circularity.words: Flourishing becomes circular when the selected goal alone justifies both ethical action and the normative authority of pursuing that goal.
con-flourishing-goal-circularity.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly distinguishes using flourishing to evaluate actions from justifying why flourishing should govern evaluation, exposing a genuine foundational burden for the secular case. Principal limitation: It represents the opposing justification as bare repetition without establishing that no constitutive, experiential, reciprocal, or reflective reasons support concern for human interests. Live burden: The objection must engage those stronger reasons, identify precisely where their normative bridge fails, and show that Christian value grounding escapes an analogous dependence on foundational commitments. Locked score: The mixed band reflects high central relevance and a clearly recoverable challenge, but also materially overstated certainty, incomplete contact with conditional objectivity, limited evidence, and insufficiently charitable treatment of the available secular justification.

con-christian-foundations-comparative-ca.words: Christianity proposes God’s character as a unified, nonarbitrary foundation for ethics, logic, science, and intelligibility in comparative worldview assessment.
con-christian-foundations-comparative-ca.critique: Strongest feature: The closing unifies ethics, logic, science, and intelligibility under a single proposed Christian foundation and explicitly reconnects those domains to the motion-level comparison. Principal limitation: It principally restates exclusivity without defending revelation, uniqueness, epistemic access, alternative comparison, or the practical reliability needed to resolve disagreement and improve decisions. Live burden: The case must establish its divine premises, derive the relevant norms and scientific presuppositions, confront serious secular alternatives, and demonstrate superior conflict resolution. Locked score: The mixed band reflects exceptional motion relevance and an intelligible organizing proposal, but substantial deductions follow from categorical overstatement, missing inferential bridges, limited charity, low evidentiary support, and unanswered practical components of the comparative burden.

strengths: Established flourishing and empirically informed interests as a clear common domain for comparison.
Presented contextual revision and disaster exceptions as concrete advantages of a consequence-sensitive moral method.
Answered foundational attacks with a strong distinction between using logic reliably and explaining its ultimate origin.
Combined fallibility, logical testing, experienced reality, and independent corroboration into a practical epistemic method.
Used central Christian doctrinal disagreement to challenge scriptural conflict-resolution reliability.

blunders.text: The claim that God is merely irrelevant compressed the stronger Christian view that relationship with God constitutes flourishing.
The categorical exclusion of every secular instruction to kill or enslave exceeded the support provided by equality and autonomy.
The case clarified value-relative objectivity more successfully than it justified why flourishing should possess governing moral authority.

strengths: Made non-self-refutation a clear threshold condition for comparative intellectual adequacy.
Pressed serious questions about reliable cognition under physical causation and about science’s unproved presuppositions.
Identified the distinction between evaluating consequences and independently justifying the value used to evaluate them.
Offered New Testament revelation, divine character, and neighbor-love as substantive components of the Christian alternative.

blunders.text: The cognition objection did not establish that physically caused processes cannot track logical truth, while divine image was asserted as the alternative mechanism.
The universal-mind inference omitted acknowledged steps between abstract universality, mentality, and specifically Christian theism.
The closing claimed uniquely Christian justification without comparing serious secular alternatives or answering practical doctrinal conflict.

newArguments.title: Capability Floor Argument
newArguments.text: A public morality can begin with a capability floor rather than an undefined instruction to maximize welfare. Severe pain, coercion, deprivation, exclusion from deliberation, and destruction of basic agency predictably disable nearly every further project a person might choose. Protecting people against those conditions is therefore supported by overlapping reasons available across many conceptions of the good. This does not settle every moral dispute, but it grounds a substantial minimum while leaving higher-order disagreements open to evidence, negotiation, and revision.

novelty.explanation: The transcript did not develop a capability-floor basis for plural flourishing.

newArguments.title: Error-Cost Comparison
newArguments.text: Competing methods should be compared by their characteristic error costs, not by whether either can guarantee truth. A revisable secular procedure can require publication of reasons, independent testing, representation of affected parties, and preannounced conditions for correction. When a rule harms people or a factual premise fails, those mechanisms create identifiable paths toward amendment. A revelation-centered method may also revise interpretations, but its comparative case must specify equally public correction rules. This converts an abstract foundations dispute into a testable institutional question about detecting and repairing consequential mistakes.

novelty.explanation: The transcript did not formulate comparative superiority through institutional error costs and correction rules.

novelty.explanation: It qualifies the exclusivity claim and makes practical reliability a condition rather than an assumption.

newArguments.title: Integrated Personalism Argument
newArguments.text: Christianity can frame its comparative advantage as explanatory integration rather than a bare claim that alternatives cannot account for logic. If reality originates in a rational personal source, then intelligible order, finite rational agents, moral accountability, and relational goods belong within one explanatory pattern. That pattern does not prove Christianity merely by being unified; it must be compared with naturalist rivals for coherence, scope, simplicity, and evidential fit. The argument nevertheless avoids inferring a specifically Christian God directly from abstract universality and offers a more defensible abductive proposal.

novelty.explanation: The transcript did not present a criteria-governed abductive argument from integrated personalism.

newArguments.title: Interpretive Accountability Argument
newArguments.text: Doctrinal disagreement need not defeat revelation if Christianity supplies accountable procedures for identifying and correcting interpretation. A strengthened method would prioritize clear central teachings, read contested passages within literary and historical context, disclose theological assumptions, consult diverse communities, and test applications against the command to love one’s neighbor. Persistent disagreement would remain evidence against reliability, but not decisive evidence by itself. Christianity’s comparative burden would then become empirical and procedural: show that these practices reduce contradiction, restrain motivated interpretation, and produce durable moral cooperation better than relevant alternatives.

novelty.explanation: The transcript raised disagreement but did not construct a detailed Christian procedure for interpretive accountability.
